scope: memory_core with both blocking L1 caches (rtl/memory/l1_cache.sv, 1 KiB two-way, 32-byte lines): a read-only I$ between fetch_two_wide and the instruction port, and a write-back, write-allocate D$ between the data-port arbiter and the data port. MMIO passes through the D$ unchanged. A retired FENCE.I holds fetch, cleans the D$, invalidates the I$, then refetches. No LSQ, prefetch, hit-under-miss or coherence beyond FENCE.I.
dispatch: MEMORY_SERVICE=1 requires TRAP_SERVICE=1 (SYSTEM_SERVICE in the backend). Legal loads/stores share the solo head_dispatch descriptor with CSR/MRET/WFI/FENCE, bypass IQ, and block younger allocation. Lane-one memory waits for lane zero. At exact raw ROB head ID/PC, both saved PRF source tags are read and captured once. No speculative memory issue. FENCE and FENCE.I prepare only when memory_busy_o is clear (no owner, in-flight or canceled transaction, committed-store drain or fatal), then retire like WFI with no effects. FENCE.I completion is its accepted solo retirement: that same handshake raises the system redirect to PC+4, which empties the line buffer and marks any offered or accepted instruction request for discard; that traffic drains afterward while the new fetch waits. Younger dispatch is held from capture until that retirement. Cancellation before retirement produces no redirect.
retirement: Success uses real solo ROB/PRF retirement. Only a system result qualifies the system controller serial_accept input; memory retirement counts as ordinary minstret retirement. Faults arbitrate once on raw completion port zero and retain memory ownership until actual CSR trap acceptance. A younger memory descriptor does not gate an older nonmemory fault.
admission: DCACHE=1 enables PREFILL_STORES in the head memory path. After alignment/PMA preparation, the existing read engine checks or refills the store line before retirement. A successful read reserves the serial data path and binds the full 13-bit ID, address, data, mask and size until atomic store commit or cancellation. No competing data request or FENCE.I maintenance can evict the line; the committed write must hit. A failed refill remains at the ROB head and traps with cause 7 and the original address/PC, without writing store bytes. External admit_valid_i/admit_id_i are ignored in this mode; admission_* remains a descriptor view, not an earned-admission indication. Without DCACHE the external admission contract remains required. Dirty-victim writeback and protocol errors remain fatal.
ports: Instruction and data ports are independent memory_protocol channels. Data engines share a single arbiter. memory_issue_allowed_i authorizes new load/store-prefill/MMIO bus grants; held offers survive later permission withdrawal. Cached-store commitment is authorized by internal admission and accepted retirement, then drains independently. Cacheable-store prefill requires memory_issue_allowed_i; an integrator must eventually grant issue or cancel the unretired store. After the read is granted, permission withdrawal does not retract its request or invalidate earned admission.
recovery: flush_i requires flush_ready_o. Keep retirement/trap service available while flush_ready_o is low; caller defers flush instead of canceling irrevocable MMIO. Normal flush cancels an uncommitted owner, but offered cached reads and committed stores drain. Branch recovery can discard a younger unprepared descriptor. Internal trap recovery releases memory only on its qualified trap acceptance, without feeding that acceptance into cancel.
fatal: Either instruction or data protocol fatal freezes allocation, execution/completion acceptance, retirement, traps and redirects. Instruction fatal does not cancel memory ownership or committed writes; granted data traffic may finish, with results held until common reset. Data fatal suppresses new fetch launches while existing instruction traffic drains. Reset also resets the external targets and suppresses pre-reset responses; it does not undo prior device effects or committed writes.
drain: drained_i additionally requires memory_busy_o=0, alongside existing frontend/backend/system drain conditions. The on-chip recycle coordinator (config/fetch_execution_core.json) also waits for memory_busy_o=0 and no offered data request before its drain; generations never silently wrap.
verification: cached_core_tb.cpp reuses every memory_core scenario with ICACHE_CORE and DCACHE_CORE defined. The I$ shadow oracle checks every fetched word. The data port model serves refills and full-line writebacks from target bytes and checks MMIO bit-for-bit. Load results are checked against architectural bytes at retirement; target bytes lag the D$ and are compared after a FENCE.I clean. Added: same-set conflict evictions read back (fast and slow port), a writeback fault that freezes the core, and the D$ clean of each self-modified word. Store admission adds hit/miss checks, byte/halfword/word refill faults held through trap acceptance and retry at the same PC, cancellation/reset before grant, during stalled/accepted/coincident refill, and at held success/fault. The external monitor rejects any backing-memory request during committed-store drain; committed stores must hit the admitted line. A paired deterministic run checks identical timing with external admission absent versus asserted with alternating matching/wrong IDs, releases a delayed prefill issue grant, and places a store after a slow FENCE.I clean.
